The implementation now uses a uniform spatial hash: each point checks only the 3×3 neighborhood of its cell, and duplicate points at zero radius are counted with a frequency map. I also retained a fallback for non-finite radii so edge-case arithmetic stays aligned with the original function. Next I’m validating exact counts and timing all benchmark shapes.

The first benchmark confirms large gains on uniform and gridded data, but dense clustered data is the limiting case because many candidate pairs are genuinely close. I’m adding a safe bulk-count optimization: when a bucket’s bounding box proves every point in it is within range of the new point, the whole bucket is counted without individual distance calculations.
